solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Finish off flash young boxer? (3,2)

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, as is a flash
a boxer is a breed of dog, and a young dog is a pup

annotation.surface: A promising young fighter being told to finish off his opponent in style.
annotation.walkthrough: The boxer is not a fighter but the dog breed, which the question mark flags.
annotation.definitionFit: To mop up is to finish off the last remaining bits of a task.

entries.clue: Different name adopted by old creative force (6,6)

indicatorNotes.adopted by: an adopted child is taken into the family, so OTHER N is taken inside MATURE

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name

annotation.surface: An elderly artist who has taken on a new pseudonym.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old creative force' reads as a single phrase, but 'old' belongs to the wordplay and only 'creative force' defines.
annotation.definitionFit: Mother Nature is nature personified as the force that creates and sustains life.

entries.clue: Particular bar order maybe featuring starter of oysters (5)

indicatorNotes.featuring: a show featuring a star has it inside, so PINT holds the O
indicatorNotes.starter of: a starter is the first course, so take the first letter of oysters

blocks.note: a pint is a typical order at a bar

annotation.surface: Someone at an oyster bar being fussy about what they order first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Particular' looks like an adjective meaning fussy; it is the noun, a detail, as in 'correct in every particular'.
annotation.definitionFit: A particular is an individual item or detail, and so is a point.

entries.clue: Favourite deep or sweet, earthy smell (9)

blocks.note: the teacher's pet is the favourite
a deep colour or voice is a rich one

annotation.surface: Choosing between a favourite dark scent and a sweet one, like a perfume buyer.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition starts at 'sweet', so the 'or' is not a choice but two letters of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Petrichor is the pleasant earthy smell of rain falling on dry ground.

entries.clue: Branch of govt supporting key area of London (8)

blocks.note: to be for something is to support it

annotation.surface: A government department backing an important district of the capital.
annotation.walkthrough: The abbreviation 'govt' hints that the branch is abbreviated too. Deptford is a district of south-east London on the Thames.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the answer is one particular district, on the south bank of the Thames near Greenwich.

entries.clue: Disclaimer of note I included in business transaction (6)

indicatorNotes.included in: N and I are put inside DEAL

blocks.note: a deal is a business transaction

annotation.surface: A contract carrying a written disclaimer that the signatory insisted on adding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Note' here is the abbreviation N, not a written message, though the surface wants a note of disclaimer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are statements refusing to accept responsibility or knowledge.

entries.clue: Put dull piece of cloth on table? (5,3)

blocks.note: to put something is to place it

annotation.surface: An instruction to lay a plain, dull cloth on the table.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a place mat need not be cloth, and that the definition is loose.
annotation.definitionFit: A place mat is a small mat or cloth laid at each setting on a table.

entries.clue: Provide money for taking over institute (5)

indicatorNotes.taking: FUND takes the O in, holding it inside

blocks.note: to fund = to provide money for
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

annotation.surface: A benefactor paying to take over an institute.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Institute' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to set up.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: both mean to set up or establish, as a school or charity.

entries.clue: Drill tries to cut through concrete (9)

indicatorNotes.to cut through: HEARS cuts into REAL, ending up inside it

blocks.note: a judge tries or hears a case

annotation.surface: A builder attempting to bore a hole through concrete with a power drill.
annotation.walkthrough: The drill looks like a tool and the concrete like a building material; the drill is practice and concrete is an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym in the practice sense: a fire drill is a run-through of what to do for real.

entries.clue: In truth, Canada’s misrepresented somewhere far from Britain (7,2,5)

indicatorNotes.misrepresented: the letters are presented wrongly, in a different order

annotation.surface: A complaint that Canada is being unfairly portrayed as a remote place.
annotation.walkthrough: Tristan da Cunha is a British overseas territory in the South Atlantic, one of the most remote inhabited islands in the world.
annotation.definitionFit: The island is thousands of miles from Britain, although it is British territory.

entries.clue: Surfing location in Tenerife can ultimately get turbulent (8,4)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately = in the end, so take the last letter of get
indicatorNotes.turbulent: turbulent water is churned up, so the letters are churned

blocks.note: last letter of get, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: Tenerife's surf beaches, where the waves can get rough.
annotation.walkthrough: The surfing is on the web, not the waves: an internet cafe rents out computers by the hour.
annotation.definitionFit: A description by function: it is a shop where customers pay to browse the web.

entries.clue: Former con mostly had something for free (9)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most but not all of TRICK, so drop its last letter

blocks.note: to have something to eat is to eat it

annotation.surface: A former con artist who got his meal without paying.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For free' reads as 'without paying'; 'free' is the definition, a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: both mean to release someone from a tangle or difficulty.

entries.clue: Pipe coming from back of integrated shower (5)

indicatorNotes.back of: the back of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: a shower is a spell of rain

annotation.surface: Plumbing: the pipe leading out of the back of a built-in shower unit.
annotation.walkthrough: The shower looks like a bathroom fitting; it is weather.
annotation.definitionFit: A drain is a pipe carrying away waste water.

entries.clue: Just joking about this is disgusting — it’s of zero value (6)

annotation.definitionNote: a clause describing the answer: nought is the thing of zero value

indicatorNotes.about: NOT goes about, or around, UGH

blocks.note: the jokey 'not!' tacked on to a statement to show it was a joke
what you say when something is disgusting

annotation.surface: Someone protesting that a joke was only a joke, while dismissing something as disgusting and worthless.
annotation.walkthrough: NOT is the tag in 'That was great — not!', meaning I was only joking.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the figure 0 is the thing whose value is nothing.

entries.clue: Experienced strange urge, no end (9)

indicatorNotes.strange: the letters are put in a strange order

annotation.surface: Someone who felt a peculiar, endless urge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No end' is not a deletion instruction; its letters are part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as past participles: both mean lived through, as with an operation or ordeal.

entries.clue: Irish politician’s experience encompassing new computer-based tech (8)

indicatorNotes.encompassing: TASTE encompasses, or surrounds, N and AI

blocks.note: to have a taste of something is to experience it

annotation.surface: An Irish politician's experience with some new computer technology.
annotation.walkthrough: The Tánaiste is the deputy prime minister of Ireland. The 's is short for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: The Tánaiste is a senior Irish politician, second to the Taoiseach.

entries.clue: Divine home’s invaded by soldiers — that’s concerning (2,7)

blocks.note: Asgard is the home of the gods in Norse myth, with the S of 's
the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

annotation.surface: A worrying report that heaven itself has been invaded by troops.
annotation.walkthrough: 'That's concerning' reads as 'that is worrying'; 'concerning' is the preposition meaning about.
annotation.definitionFit: As regards and concerning both mean 'on the subject of'.

entries.clue: Cover evidence of injury, except on rear part of head (8)

indicatorNotes.rear part of: the rear of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: a scab forms over a wound
bar = except, as in 'all bar one'

annotation.surface: Covering up the signs of a head wound, except at the back.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts BAR above D. 'Cover' looks like a verb; it is the noun, a sheath.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the sheath that covers a sword's blade.

entries.clue: Swift movement of water I created when swimming (4,4)

annotation.surface: A swimmer boasting of the wash they made in the water.
annotation.walkthrough: A tide race is a fast, turbulent current where the tide runs through a narrow channel.
annotation.definitionFit: A tide race is a strong, swift tidal current.

entries.clue: Odd spots of dirt over the length of trimmed fabric (6)

indicatorNotes.Odd spots of: the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of dirt
indicatorNotes.over: DR is put over, or ahead of, the rest
indicatorNotes.trimmed: trimmed has its end cut off, so ALONG loses its G

blocks.note: first and third letters of dirt
along = over the length of, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A few stray marks of dirt spread along a strip of cut cloth.
annotation.walkthrough: Dralon is a trade name for an acrylic fibre, often made into velvety upholstery fabric.
annotation.definitionFit: Dralon is a synthetic fabric used for upholstery and curtains.

entries.clue: Times ignoring introduction of injunction is a-flipping-mazing? (6)

annotation.definitionNote: a definition by example: the clue word shows tmesis in action

indicatorNotes.ignoring: TIMES ignores, or leaves out, the I
indicatorNotes.introduction of: the introduction of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: TIMES without I, the first letter of injunction

annotation.surface: A newspaper that pays no attention to a court injunction, and how amazing that is.
annotation.walkthrough: Tmesis is splitting a word by inserting another inside it, as 'flipping' is pushed into 'amazing'.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is itself an example of tmesis, so the question mark flags a definition by example.

entries.clue: River — one in Russia not near any cities? (5)

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river
one = another river, the Ural, which flows through Russia

annotation.surface: A remote Russian river far from any towns.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One' stands for a second river, so the clue needs two: the abbreviation R and the Ural.
annotation.definitionFit: Rural areas are countryside, away from towns and cities.

entries.clue: You’re talking about eating eventually? (5)

indicatorNotes.about: about = turned round, so the hidden letters read backwards
indicatorNotes.eating: the phrase eats, or holds inside it, the letters wanted

blocks.note: five letters hidden across the join: you-RE TAL-king

annotation.surface: Someone asking whether the conversation is about when dinner will finally happen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eating' looks like the topic of conversation; it signals letters held inside 'You're talking', which then read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean at some time after now.

entries.clue: By all means, stay overnight! (2,2,5)

blocks.note: an invitation from a host, read literally

annotation.surface: A generous host urging a visitor to stay the night.
annotation.walkthrough: The same phrase serves twice: once as the idiom of permission, once as a literal invitation to be a houseguest.
annotation.definitionFit: Both halves are things you might say with the words 'be my guest'.

entries.clue: Periodically excels at providing razzle-dazzle (5)

indicatorNotes.Periodically: at regular intervals, so every other letter of excels

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters of excels

annotation.surface: A performer who now and then shines with showy brilliance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' applies only to 'excels'; 'at' is taken whole.
annotation.definitionFit: Éclat is conspicuous brilliance or showy success, which is razzle-dazzle.

entries.clue: Revised tutorial has to cover a US state (5,9)

indicatorNotes.Revised: a revised text is rewritten, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.to cover: the rearranged letters cover, or surround, A US

annotation.surface: An updated study guide about one of the American states.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A US state' looks like a single phrase; the state is Australian, and 'a US' is wordplay held inside the shuffled letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: one of Australia's six states, with Adelaide its capital.

entries.clue: Guy journeys round British islands (8)

indicatorNotes.round: HE RIDES goes round the B

blocks.note: a guy is a man, he

annotation.surface: A man travelling around the islands of Britain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Guy journeys' makes the sentence 'he rides', and B sits between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: The Hebrides are island groups off the west coast of Scotland.

entries.clue: Scorer in South American cup match (5)

blocks.note: a cup tie is a knockout match in a cup competition

annotation.surface: A goalscorer in a South American cup game.
annotation.walkthrough: The scorer is not a goalscorer but a composer, one who writes scores: Erik Satie. A cup tie is a British term for a knockout-cup football match.
annotation.definitionFit: Satie was a French composer, and a composer is someone who writes scores.
